subject.title: Telegram: support fail-closed unknown-group handling with optional auto-leave

question: Should OpenClaw accept an opt-in Telegram unknown-group action config that can warn and leave non-allowlisted groups, and should the paired PR be revised as that implementation path?
rationale: The request adds new user-facing config and a security-sensitive channel side effect, so automation cannot choose the permanent product/security semantics.

options.title: Revise the paired Telegram PR
options.body: Use the existing implementation candidate as the starting point, but require precise unknown-group classification, docs/schema alignment, conflict resolution, and real Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Keep deny-only behavior
options.body: Decline warn/leave config for now and keep current fail-closed deny/log behavior as the supported Telegram posture.

options.title: Fold into broader group security work
options.body: Defer this narrow auto-leave request into the broader pairing/audit direction tracked by related group security issues.

recommendation.title: Revise the paired Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use the existing implementation candidate as the starting point, but require precise unknown-group classification, docs/schema alignment, conflict resolution, and real Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Telegram authorization and handler surfaces most closely trace through Peter Steinberger's group-policy and handler refactors.
